I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** Every production region (us-east, us-west, eu-west) was on v2.3.1, the latest release. It was failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%. Its release candidate had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. A human approver signed off on the rollback. Afterwards, all three regions report v2.3.0, health checks pass and the error rate is about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 records what failed, the rollback and the current healthy status. It notes that the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before v2.3.1 is deployed again. My first attempt to create it timed out. I checked the incident list, confirmed nothing had been created, and tried again with the same deduplication key, so there's only one incident.

content.text:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** Every production region (us-east, us-west, eu-west) was on v2.3.1, the latest release. It was failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%. Its release candidate had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. A human approver signed off on the rollback. Afterwards, all three regions report v2.3.0, health checks pass and the error rate is about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 records what failed, the rollback and the current healthy status. It notes that the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before v2.3.1 is deployed again. My first attempt to create it timed out. I checked the incident list, confirmed nothing had been created, and tried again with the same deduplication key, so there's only one incident.
